mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision triggers a risk-off reaction, depressing near-term equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the preceding month
regime_hint: tightening phase of the Fed funds rate
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-tightening baseline (p > 0.1) during the identified trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) above 200,000 in the prior month signals labor market strength, which is associated with higher consumer confidence and thus positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite PAYEMS > 200000 for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in RSAFS (durable goods orders) of more than 2% in the prior month indicates weakening demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as market anticipates softening economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >2% in the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.15) during the identified contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in INDPRO (industrial production) above 2% for two consecutive months suggests supply chain expansion, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as market anticipates continued output growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative over the 2-month expansion window (mean ratio ≤ 1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained dual decline in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months indicates a disinflationary and easing environment, producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% increase AND FEDFUNDS < 3% increase for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.1) during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% signals tight labor markets, which typically precede positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors price in wage growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.15) during the tightening episode.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of HOUST (housing starts) below 1.2 million indicate a cooling housing market, which predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as risk aversion rises.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 1.2 million for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) during the cooling period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 (GDP) of over 1% for three months suggests economic softness, which is associated with negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as investors anticipate weaker growth.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain flat or positive despite three months of GDP declines >1%.
